prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

TEXT_C:
Summary of proposals and positions (ideology removed)

- European Union and currency
  - Withdraw from the EU; repeal the European Communities Act 1972.
  - Negotiate trade agreements with European states and others; keep the pound permanently.
  - Maintain Bank of England interest-rate independence.

- Economy, trade, and regulation
  - Pursue global free trade, deepen ties with Commonwealth and North America.
  - Large-scale deregulation, prioritising small and medium-sized enterprises; review metrication and abattoir rules.
  - Simplify and reduce taxes: raise the income tax threshold to remove ~1 million low earners from tax, reform inheritance and capital gains taxes, consider replacing VAT with a retail sales tax after EU exit.
  - Oppose tax harmonisation.

- Independence Dividend (estimated ~£20bn annually)
  - Savings from ending EU budget contributions and gains from deregulation and growth.
  - Planned allocations include: agriculture (£2bn), regional support (£1bn), state pension uplift (£2.8bn), elderly care (£0.5bn), restoring frozen expat pensions (£0.3bn), tax changes (£2.7bn total), NHS (£2bn) plus nursing pay (£0.5bn), 30,000 more teachers (£1.2bn), 25,000 more police (£0.8bn), fuel duty cut (9p/litre; ~£3.7bn), defence (£2.5bn).

- Health and social care
  - Increase NHS funding; restore clearer hospital management roles (e.g., matron-style leadership), reduce bureaucracy, focus on infection control and patient care.
  - Improve nurse pay and retention; rebalance training toward practical competence; recruit internationally where needed.
  - Review and simplify social services; reduce bureaucracy and focus on practical outcomes.

- Welfare and pensions
  - Simplify benefits to reduce fraud and administration; ensure work always pays.
  - Consider basic income-style support for specific groups to aid re-entry to work.
  - Raise state pension by £5/week; increase elderly care funding; restore full pensions to affected expatriates.
  - Explore partial diversion of National Insurance into personal pension funds (grandfathering existing pensioners).

- Education
  - Allow selection/streaming; target class sizes under 25; hire more teachers; elevate technical/vocational routes; consider vouchers; encourage specialist and single-sex or faith options where desired.
  - Reform teacher training toward proven methods; address discipline and attainment gaps.
  - Protect school sports and halt sale of playing fields.
  - Support independent funding models for higher education; encourage private universities with scholarships; treat overseas students equally by origin.

- Transport and environment
  - Integrated transport; case-by-case approach to ownership/privatisation; oppose part-sale of London Underground.
  - Reduce fuel duty; fund bypasses, route upgrades, maintenance, cycle lanes; adjust vehicle tax by emissions.
  - Decentralise environmental enforcement to local authorities; strengthen monitoring of pollution-related health impacts.
  - Strong GMO labelling and protections; encourage renewables (biofuels, wave, wind, solar, hydrogen).

- Home affairs, justice, and rights
  - Protect jury trial and common-law safeguards; oppose EU-wide legal and policing integration.
  - Repeal and reenact the Human Rights Act to align with domestic legal tradition.
  - Increase police numbers; prioritise visible, community-linked policing; use rehabilitation and non-custodial sentences for non-violent offences; “life means life” for the most serious crimes.

- Immigration and asylum
  - Skills-based immigration model; equalise treatment for family reunification compared with non-EU countries.
  - Speed up asylum processing with reception centres; tighten monitoring; prioritise first safe country principles; seek reform of the 1951 Refugee Convention.

- Agriculture and fisheries
  - Replace CAP with national policy; introduce voluntary Land Management Contracts paying for agreed environmental and land-use outcomes; support organics and higher welfare; assist young farmers; enable diversification and farmers’ markets.
  - Amend right-to-roam to reflect local conditions.
  - Exit the Common Fisheries Policy; exclusive national control up to 200 miles under international law; create recovery zones and ban damaging methods; allow access via bilateral agreements.

- Defence and foreign affairs
  - Increase defence spending on personnel and equipment; prioritise NATO; leave EU defence structures.
  - Pursue cost-effective procurement, including from the US.
  - Refocus aid toward communities, with governance and freedom conditions.

- Constitution and governance
  - Enact a UK Bill of Rights preventing transfer of sovereignty without consent.
  - Strengthen Parliament over the executive; empower select committees; review quangos.
  - Oppose regionalisation; consider a further Welsh referendum; address West Lothian question; restore county-based local government; enable citizen-initiated local referenda with an impartial referendum commission.

TEXT_F:
Summary of 2001 manifesto proposals (ideological framing and names omitted)

- Family and education
  - Targeted tax cuts: higher Children’s Tax Credit for under‑5s; transferable allowance for couples with young children or caring responsibilities; remove tax on Widowed Parent benefits; reform in‑work credit to be paid to the caring parent.
  - School autonomy (“Free Schools”): heads/governors control staffing, pay, admissions via home–school agreements; easier exclusion for disruptive pupils with off-site Progress Centres; successful schools free to expand; new schools allowed from faith, parent, charitable and company providers; parents can trigger special inspections and management change; redirect bureaucracy savings directly to schools.
  - Students and universities: raise loan repayment threshold to £20,000; no top‑up fees; create university endowments.

- Crime and justice
  - Increase police numbers; cut bureaucracy; visible policing (e.g., paperwork done on the beat); parish constables; focus on antisocial behaviour.
  - Expand secure training places for persistent young offenders; link release to behaviour/qualifications.
  - Mandatory prison for selling drugs to under‑16s; tougher sentences near schools.
  - End automatic early release; require prison work with proceeds to victims/families.
  - Lifetime supervision available for sex offenders; protect children online.
  - Stronger victim rights: named contacts in police/CPS; written reasons if charges dropped; update self‑defence and double jeopardy rules.

- Economy and regulation
  - Tax reductions funded by £8bn in savings (excluding schools/NHS/police/defence): abolish taxes on most savings/dividends; raise pensioner personal allowance by £2,000; married couple’s allowance; higher Children’s Tax Credit for under‑5s; cut fuel duty by at least 6p/litre; business rates cuts; abolish IR35; targeted regeneration breaks; relief for approved share options.
  - Simpler, more transparent tax/accounts; Capital Gains Tax simplification with lower rates.
  - Deregulation Commission with departmental regulatory budgets; small-firm exemptions; focus utility regulators on competition.
  - Replace Climate Change Levy package; review nuclear’s role.
  - Keep the pound; bolster monetary policy independence; external fiscal scrutiny.

- Health
  - Match planned NHS funding but shift control to clinicians; Patient’s Guarantee of maximum waits based on clinical need with right to alternative NHS/private provision; more choice for patients/GPs; empower ward sisters/matrons; expand practice nurse roles; specialist surgical units; Exceptional Medicines Fund; increase hospice funding; remove tax penalties on private medical insurance when affordable.

- Older people and care
  - Raise basic state pension (larger uplift for over‑75s); option to consolidate certain payments into a higher tax‑free pension; increase age allowance by £2,000 to remove ~1m from income tax; abolish compulsory annuitisation at 75; explore funded pension option for younger workers; protect assets for those who pre‑fund long‑term care.

- International and defence
  - In the EU but retain veto; keep the pound; seek treaty flexibility/reserved powers; strengthen the single market and anti‑fraud measures.
  - Prioritise NATO; oppose separate EU military structures; maintain independent deterrent; support missile defence; reach full manning; reserves reform; exempt armed forces from certain human rights constraints as other states do.
  - Aid: work toward 0.7% GNP; double share via charities; improve EU aid or permit bilateral alternatives; push debt relief, HIV/AIDS, conflict resolution; envoy for religious freedom.
  - Trade: pursue EU‑NAFTA free trade area toward global free trade by 2020; align diplomacy and trade promotion.

- Asylum
  - House new applicants in secure reception centres pending decisions; presume refusal for safe‑country claims; create a removals agency for rejected cases.

- Welfare and civil society
  - Office of Civil Society; eliminate irrecoverable VAT for charities.
  - Replace existing job schemes with outcome‑based contracts paying for sustained employment; “can work, must work” principle; lone parents with children over 11 to seek suitable work.
  - Improve disabled savings rules; new Incapacity Benefit agency funding rehabilitation; national anti‑fraud squad; clean up National Insurance numbers.

- Town, country, transport, environment
  - Foot‑and‑mouth recovery plan; reform CAP/CFP with more national/local control; honest food labelling; reduce rural red tape; cut business rates for key rural services; benefit card to sustain post offices; support rural transport.
  - Abolish top‑down housebuilding targets; more local control; protect green/“blue belt” areas; rural affairs select committee.
  - Urban regeneration companies with powers over policing, schools, planning, and housing renewal; promote brownfield building; expand homeownership (right‑to‑buy, rent‑to‑mortgage, homesteading).
  - Transport: long‑term plans; Roads Standards Unit; consider 80mph where safe with strict enforcement; charge foreign lorries; revive rail; cut fuel duty; promote cleaner fuels/vehicles.
  - Environment: emissions trading, conservation, renewables, cleaner generation.

- Culture, media, sport
  - Privatise Channel 4; £3bn endowment for cultural bodies; simplify lottery rules; strengthen tourism promotion.
  - Protect school sport time/playing fields; charitable status for local sports clubs; streamline funding.
  - Single media/communications regulator; modernise ownership rules; independent BBC regulation; fair access for religious broadcasters.

- Democracy and governance
  - Devolve powers to high‑performing “free councils”; fewer central targets; local referendums on large council tax rises.
  - Abolish regional agencies/assemblies; return development powers locally.
  - English votes for English laws; strengthen Lords with independent appointments and elected element; enhance Commons scrutiny (more frequent PM accountability, stronger select committees); retain current general election voting system.
  - Reduce numbers of ministers, MPs (after scrutiny reforms), and political advisers.
